newsitem.title: UK: Soaring dollar pushes Gold to 40-month low fix.
newsitem.headline: Soaring dollar pushes Gold to 40-month low fix.

text.p: The world price of gold slipped briefly below the $350 per ounce support level on Wednesday morning before fixing at its lowest level since September 1993 under pressure from a soaring dollar.
Elsewhere in commodity markets world coffee prices soared almost six percent on news of a possible fall in Colombian coffee exports as a strike at Colombia's Buenaventura port entered its eigth day.
March delivery Robusta grade coffee on the London futures market closed at $1,545 a tonne on the Colombian news and fund buying, up from Tuesday's four-month high of $1,473.
Colombian January coffee exports may be 300,000 bags less than anticipated, Colombia's National Coffee Grower's Federation said.
Analysts said gold's fall was due to a firmer dollar, which hit a 31-month high against the mark during morning trading, and continuing fears of central bank gold sales.
Gold later bounced and fixed just above the psychological $350 level at $351.20 per ounce, and closed at $350.85, sharply down on Tuesday's $352.75.
Platinum continued its downward trend to close at a fresh three-year low of $356.50 per ounce but silver recovered from an early dip to close at $4.72 per ounce, down a cent.

Base metals were reluctant to break out of recent ranges during the midsession, though many maintained an upside bias. Copper failed to overcome resistance at around $2,280, and closed up $10 on Tuesday, at $2265 per tonne.
Tin remained little changed above $6,000 per tonne, while aluminium hovered around resistance levels.

London March futures for the world benchmark Brent Blend of crude oil were steadied at higher levels on a midday technical correction, and closed at $22.44 per barrel, one cent down on Tuesday's close of $22.45.
Chicago wheat futures were lower on profit taking, after warmer weather in the U.S. winter wheat growing region diminished concerns of crop damage.
Some leading commodity prices at 1715 GMT -
